title: MemPalace
by: MemPalace, the open-source Python project (first published under milla-jovovich/mempalace, now the MemPalace org); MIT licensed. Read from its README and three pages of its website source (concepts/knowledge-graph, concepts/the-palace, reference/mcp-tools). Its benchmark files were not read.
summary: A local memory that stores conversations verbatim, never summarised, filed in a hierarchy of wings (people, projects), rooms (topics) and drawers (original text). Beside it is a small temporal graph in SQLite whose facts have a validity window. Agents use it through about 48 MCP tools, including add, invalidate and supersede for graph facts.
ideas: Verbatim first: the stored text is the original; search returns it as written.
Graph facts are subject, predicate, object with valid_from and valid_to; valid_to empty means still current.
Three distinct writes: add a fact that can coexist, invalidate a fact that ended, supersede a single-valued fact.
supersede closes the old fact and opens the new one in one transaction at the same boundary, so a query at that moment returns only the new value.
Each graph fact links back to the verbatim memory it came from (source_closet) and carries a confidence.
Updating a drawer first appends the old text to drawer_revisions.jsonl; if that append fails, the update is refused.
Identical content gets a deterministic id and is skipped; a separate check finds near-duplicates before filing.

took.idea: Separate writes for 'add', 'ended' and 'replaced', not one generic update
A replacement closes the old and opens the new in one atomic write
History is appended before any change, and the change fails if the append fails
